newsitem.title: UK: Guinness in mega merger after 248 years.
newsitem.headline: Guinness in mega merger after 248 years.

text.p: Guinness Plc, the British brewer and spirits group which announced a multi-billion pound merger with rival Grand Metropolitan Plc on Monday, can trace its roots back over 245 years.

Formed in 1759 in Dublin, Ireland, Guinness spent its first 230 years as a brewer before expanding into the world of spirits, concocting a drinks giant boasting brands such as Johnnie Walker and Bell's Scotch whisky, Draught Guinness and Moet & Chandon champagne.
Incorporated as Arthur Guinness Son & Co Ltd in 1886, the company changed its name from Arthur Guinness & Sons Plc to Guinness Plc in 1985.
Here is a summary of its main deals to date.

1986 -- launches what becomes known as the "infamous" acquisition of whisky group Distillers Plc. The deal later led to Britain's highest-profile fraud trial and landed former Guinness chairman Earnest Saunders in jail, convicted on 12 counts including false accounting and theft for inflating Guinness' share price to help the takeover. At 2.7 billion pounds ($4.4 billion), the bid is Britain's biggest takeover to date and takes time to digest.
1988 -- Guinness forms a key alliance with French luxury goods and drinks group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton. The partnership begins with a 12 percent cross shareholding.
1990 -- the cross shareholding with LVMH is increased to 24 percent.

1990/91 -- Guinness buys Cruzcampo, Spain's biggest brewer; a 50 percent stake in Australia's Bundaberg Rum Company; Pampero, Venezuela's leading rum producer; premium brandy producer Asbach Austria GmbH and Glenmore, one of America's leading domestic spirits producers.
1994 -- buys a 51 percent stake in Jamaican brewer Desnoes and Geddis.
1994 -- the LVMH alliance is unscrambled, leaving Guinness owning 34 percent of Moet Hennessy, the world's leading champagne and cognac brands. LVMH holds a 14.2 percent stake in Guinness.
1997 -- Guinness merges with Grand Metropolitan in a deal worth over 20 billion pounds.
